## What's new

### Updates from inside the app
Larvyn now checks for new releases when it starts and every few hours. When one is out, a notice offers **Update now** (downloads it, verifies the checksum, replaces Larvyn and restarts it) or **What's new**. You can also check by hand in **Settings → About & feedback**, or turn the automatic check off there.

> Coming from beta 4 or older? Run the install command below once more. From now on Larvyn updates itself.

### Reporting a bug is one click away
- **Report a bug** sits in the title bar, always visible. It opens a GitHub issue with your Larvyn version and system already filled in. The 💡 next to it requests a feature.
- Every error notification has a **Report this** link that pastes the error into the report.
- **Feedback** in the status bar and **Help & feedback** in the command palette (type `bug` or `feature`) do the same, plus a link to Discussions.

### Logos for your tools
Agents, the toolchain in Settings and the frontend and package chips in Overview now show each tool's logo (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity, Cursor, Pi, PHP, Composer, Node, Vite, React, Tailwind, Livewire, Inertia and more).

### Antigravity CLI replaces Gemini CLI
Google moved Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI (`agy`). Larvyn now detects and launches `agy`, passing your prompt with `agy -i`.

## Fixes
- **Agents and Node not found when Larvyn is opened from the app menu** (Linux and macOS). Larvyn now loads the PATH of your login shell, so tools installed through nvm, fnm, bun or npm globals (codex, opencode, node…) are found, without delaying startup.
- **Missing icon on Linux.** The window carries its own icon, and the installer registers it where every desktop finds it. Run the install command again to fix an existing install.
- **"There are no commands defined in the dev namespace" on Laravel 12 and older.** Larvyn only asks for `dev:list` when the framework has it (Laravel 13), so older apps no longer get that error in `storage/logs/laravel.log`.
- **Notifications showing twice.** An identical notification is never stacked again, and clicking a command button twice no longer starts the command twice.
- **"Could not read test results: EOF".** When a test run stops before writing its report, the Tests view says so and offers to run them again instead of showing an error.
